IC1.IC1.1: Ambulatory status (outpatient) at time of consent

IC.IC3: Clinical diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder

IC4.IC4.1: IQ greater than or equal to 70

IC5.IC5.1: Score greater than 8 on Children's Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale

IC6.IC6.1: Free of psychoactive medication for at least: one month for fluoxetine;
IC6.IC6.2: two weeks for other SSRIs and neuroleptics;
IC6.IC6.3: and five days for stimulants prior to MRI scanning [excepting stable doses (greater than three months duration) of anticonvulsant medication for seizure disorder]

EC1.EC1.1: Age less than 10 years or greater than 55 years, at time of consent

EC.EC3: Uncontrolled epilepsy (seizure within 6 months prior to consent)

EC4.EC4.1: Presence of medical conditions that might interfere with participation, or where participation would be contraindicated

EC5.EC5.1: History of neurological injury: head trauma, poorly-controlled seizure disorder (seizure within the preceding six months), stroke, prior neurosurgery, or under the care of a neurologist or neurosurgeon as determined by interview

EC7.EC7.1: Implanted or irremovable metal in the body (including certain tattoos and permanent make-up)

EC8.EC8.1: Current pregnancy (as verified by testing prior to both initial dose administration of citalopram or placebo and prior to magnetic resonance imaging) due to the risk that may be associated with SSRI treatment and magnetic resonance imaging on fetal health

EC9.EC9.1: Medical contraindications to SSRI therapy as determined by history (including induction of mania or hypomania during SSRI therapy, or known drug allergy)

EC10.EC10.1: Concomitant medication that would interfere with study participation

EC11.EC11.1: Prior history of citalopram treatment failure at appropriate doses and duration

EC12.EC12.1: Prior history of treatment failure to two previous SSRI trials at appropriate doses and duration

EC13.EC13.1: Ongoing need for psychoactive medication other than study medication [excepting stable doses (greater than three months duration) of anticonvulsant medication for seizure disorder, or diphenhydramine (Benadryl®) for sleep]
